## AFGHANISTAN — profile (page 120)

- Header facts: Region: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan; income group: Low-income; lending category: IDA; data status: Estimated data (E); population: 43.8 million; GNI: 17,855; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock, 2025: 3,419; change from 2024: +2.2%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 2015 = 2,597; 2025 = 3,419. The line is roughly flat at first, rises slightly to ≈2017, dips slightly through ≈2019, then climbs strongly to a peak around ≈2022, falls somewhat in ≈2023, is broadly steady/slightly up in ≈2024, dips slightly, and ends a little higher in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 3,419
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 2,930
  - Private nonguaranteed: 18
  - Short-term: 471

  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 1,941
    - Bilateral: 989

  - Multilateral:
    - IMF-SDR allocations: 638
    - Asian Dev. Bank: 514
    - Other multilateral: 789

  - Bilateral:
    - Russian Federation: 849
    - Saudi Arabia: 79
    - Other bilateral: 61

- Figure 3 Debt ratios:
  - External debt / exports: 177%; change: +24.3%; trend: rises modestly to ≈2017, declines to ≈2019, then rises by 2020. No data values after 2020.
  - External debt / GNI: 19%; change: -5.8%; trend: low and fairly flat through ≈2021, jumps in ≈2022, then declines through 2024.
  - Debt service / exports: 3%; change: -10.1%; trend: edges up to ≈2017, then trends downward to 2020. No data values after 2020.
  - Debt service / GNI: 0.4%; change: +49.8%; trend: broadly flat at a low level through ≈2022, dips slightly, then rises by 2024.
